justification: A dies on ‘at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute’ — the payment turns on a threshold count of sailings, not on how far behind the average sailing berths. B dies on ‘Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment’ against ‘in 2016 the relief boat’s passenger certificate ran out’ — the clause predates the withdrawal by five years. D dies on ‘A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether’ and the Q1 2023 case (forty-one sailings lost, reliability ninety-seven per cent, ‘the highest it had ever been’) — cancellations help the figure and nothing reduces the payment. Key C: ‘taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters’ = unpaid in one quarter of six years.

B dies on ‘Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes’ — 2005 intervals were twenty-five, and the seventy is the one-boat present. C dies on absence (Cottam says nothing about loading in 2005) and on the reverse direction of the only berth-work fact: the linkspan rebuilt in 2013 adds ‘a manufacturer’s ninety seconds at each berth’, so that work is longer now, not then. D dies on ‘The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005’ and Cottam’s own ‘The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking’ — lateness was being measured in 2005; the 2012 stamp series is Cattermay’s series, not the first measurement. Key A: eighteen booked against a twenty-four-minute median.

A dies on ‘The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out’ — the first padding preceded the withdrawal. B dies on the stated cause, ‘the relief boat’s passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her’ — no span links the padded book to the boat’s workload, and the text never hints the second boat was idle. C dies on ‘Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was’ with ‘the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two’ in 2013 — the stretching began pre-withdrawal. Key D: timetable took the interval 25→32, the boat’s loss took it 32→70 (‘One boat gives you one every seventy’), so the withdrawal removed the larger share of departures.

A dies on ‘Nobody disputes the stamps’ and ‘does not contest the fifteen minutes’ — the writer treats her minutes as the firmest fact in the piece, not as showing little. C dies on ‘The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well’ — he does not take her to have shown the timetable at fault at all; ‘though not by how much’ lures on her own ‘a range, not a number’. D dies on both halves: ‘Nobody disputes the stamps’ (he does not doubt her numbers) and the same ‘would bear either of the other two just as well’ (he does not grant the timetable is probably to blame). Key B: numbers accepted, cause withheld — ‘Where Cattermay’s case thins is the join.’

A dies on scope: the padding — the opening frame (‘booked to sit there’, eighteen→twenty-seven) — is missing, and nobody argues about what passengers ‘notice’; the quarrel is which cause the stamps bear. B dies on scope: it is paragraph four alone; the reliability figure, the stamps, Cottam and the writer’s weighing lie outside it. C dies on scope and slant: it is Cattermay’s paragraph alone and adopts her reading as the text’s, when the writer says ‘the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well’. Key D covers the frame (seventy-one→ninety-six per cent while thirty-nine→fifty-four minutes) and the three-way quarrel over the join.

A ‘hasty’ dies collocationally — hasty describes a rushed or careless single act, never sustained commerce; ‘does a hasty trade’ is not English. B ‘rapid’ dies collocationally — ‘does a rapid trade’ is not idiomatic; rapid names the speed of a process, not the liveliness of business. C ‘swift’ is the nearest live alternative but dies on the same ground plus context: swift is the speed of a quick single action, while the gap spans hours (‘from eleven until the light goes’) and needs liveliness of business — ‘does a brisk trade’ (key D) is the fixed collocation.

A ‘lie’ dies grammatically — ‘had lie’ is not a form. C ‘laid’ dies — past participle of transitive ‘lay’, which needs an object; the chairs ‘had lain there’ is intransitive, so ‘had laid there’ is the classic error, not a second answer in a text of this register. D ‘lay’ dies — simple past, not a participle; ‘had lay’ is ungrammatical. Key B ‘lain’ is the only past participle of intransitive ‘lie’ that fits ‘had ___ there since breakfast’.

A ‘In principle’ dies on direction: the sentence after the gap states the pitch’s actual de-facto role (‘the one staffed thing on the mile … the one person on it who is stationary and paid’), the reality side of the contrast announced by ‘What the pitch charges for and what it does are not the same thing’; the formal side is already given by ‘The hire is the whole of the transaction’. B ‘In addition’ is the nearest survivor but dies on that same structural cue: the paragraph is explicitly built as charges-for versus does, and ‘the whole of the transaction’ is a restrictive claim the next sentence must qualify, not extend — an additive marker breaks the announced contrast. D ‘In short’ dies — the sentence after the gap does not summarize the sentence before it (a ten-pence rise in a decade); it introduces new content. Key C ‘In practice’.

findings: D: ‘confesses’ is a live near-synonym of the key — ‘Pressed on whether she minds the questions, she confesses that in August they are an interruption …’ is grammatical, idiomatic and register-appropriate; it is killed by nuance (confess = own up to something personal or discreditable; concede = grant a point under pressure) and by the coda ‘a description rather than a complaint’, not by a hard textual span.
justification: B ‘boasts’ dies — the content is not self-praise and the coda calls it description. C ‘volunteers’ dies on ‘Pressed on’ — a volunteered remark is unprompted; this one was extracted under pressure. D ‘confesses’: best case — British ‘I confess’ is frequently light; she is pressed and admits that the questions are an interruption in August, and the author then softens it as description; nothing in the sentence is ungrammatical or unidiomatic with ‘confesses’. Against D — ‘confess’ frames the object as a personal admission of minding, which is exactly what ‘a description rather than a complaint’ denies, and the second half of the object (‘by late September most of the job’) is not confession-shaped; ‘concede’ pairs with ‘Pressed on’ as the standard journalistic collocation (pressed → conceded) and fits the grant-then-reframe structure. Key A is the best answer, but D is survivable with effort and its kill is a subtle reading; flag, not kill.

A ‘widely’ dies on ‘but’ and ‘it shut after its second summer’ — the clause must explain failure despite being well signed and free. B ‘scantily’ has the right direction but dies collocationally — ‘scantily’ collocates with clad/dressed/furnished, not with ‘used’; the word for this slot would be ‘sparsely’ or ‘little’, and neither is offered. C ‘strongly’ dies on both direction and collocation (‘strongly used’ is not English). Key D ‘barely used’.

Mechanism check: physically correct — diamond meshes under tow tension elongate along the tow axis and close laterally (‘every mesh pulls long and thin’, ‘a slot by then’), so a round-bodied haddock cannot get its width through, and hanging the same twine on the bar (‘turned right round the bag’) gives square meshes that stay open under drag; the key is not backwards. A dies on ‘A whole spring on, the boxes at the harbour looked much as they had the year before’ — a season, not a single trip. B dies on ‘The plaice were much as before’ — the text asserts no change, B asserts one (in the world square mesh does tend to cut flatfish escape, so B is world-plausible but text-contradicted; fair). C dies on ‘The second change was to the hanging, not the size’ — size came first. Key D matches ‘Tow it, and every mesh pulls long and thin … A haddock is round, and it has to get its width through.’

B dies on ‘Each of the first masters went on enrolling boys of his own for years afterwards’. C dies on ‘Of the five fathers, two lived in the town, one farmed nine miles off, one combed wool in the next county, and one the clerk left unplaced’ — not the five. D dies on ‘In three of the five the second premium was the larger sum’ and on Ward’s own eleven→fourteen pounds. Key A: each second binding ‘ran its seven years from the day of sealing’ and ‘fell three to six years after the first’, so it ends three to six years past the day the first term would have ended.

A dies: ‘tvärs över bäcken ovanför myren’ is where the dämme lay (‘Ett dämme av torv, ris och sten lades tvärs över bäcken ovanför myren’), not the ränna, which runs ‘tvärs över sluttningen’. B dies on ‘på de mindre anläggningarna efter ögonmått’. D dies on ‘i stället för att följa den till den lägsta punkten och skära sig ner där’ — the rule exists to prevent exactly that. Key C: ‘rännan skulle luta mindre än marken nedanför den’, illustrated by huvudrännan falling ‘drygt en halv meter på fyrahundra’ against a surface falling ‘ungefär det dubbla’.

A dies on ‘Bäckvatten från myrmark är brunt och slamfattigt. Någon nämnvärd mängd mineraljord avlagrades inte’. C inverts the mechanism and dies on ‘Rinnande vatten tillför hela tiden syre till det översta markskiktet’ with the contrast ‘Stillastående vatten gör tvärtom: det stänger ute luften’ — the text makes oxygen supply decisive, not oxygen consumption (aerobic decay does consume oxygen in the world, so C is world-plausible but not what the text presents as cause; fair). D dies on ‘halten av löst näring i vattnet var för låg för att ensam förklara skördeökningen’. Key B: ‘Det avgörande var syret … nedbrytningen av torven går fortare, och den näring som frigörs ur myren själv blir tillgänglig för växterna.’

A dies: ‘Den höll i tolv år’ is the agreement’s lifetime, not the meadows’ — ‘När och varför bruket upphörde är omtvistat’. B dies on absence — the agreement ‘fördelade vattnet’, nothing about hay. C dies: the ‘niohundra dagsverken’ is a separate uppgift (‘uppges ha tagit’), not drawn from the agreement. Key D: the agreement is introduced under ‘Till detta kom samordningen’ and ‘angav i vilken ordning turerna skulle tas’.

B dies on ‘När och varför bruket upphörde är omtvistat’ and on the two distinct causes offered (fodret upphörde att vara knappt vs arbetskraften drogs till sågverken och till Amerika). C dies: they read different material — her timings across ett fyrtiotal socknar from dikningshandlingar vs his ‘karterat rännsystemen i fyra socknar’. D’s premise (many more parishes) is verbatim-true but its causal claim ‘bottnar i’ dies: Nolvide’s objection is selection (‘valda bland dem som har bevarade dikningshandlingar’), not sample size, and Pärlhage’s is map datability (‘sällan går att tidfästa närmare än ett par decennier’) — neither roots the dispute in the count. Key A: both objections concern what the sources can bear, sealed by ‘ingen förde bok över hur många dagar som gick åt till rännorna’.

A dies on ‘oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen’. B dies on the arithmetic the text invites (‘Räkna gärna själv’): 10 800/4 = 2 700 kr per household at Kvillnäs against 3 600/24 = 150 at Ulvbråt, and on ‘gynnar den som bor glest, och det är vi som bor glest’ — reversed. D dies on ‘Den plogningen har för övrigt aldrig legat i bidraget utan i kommunens avtal med entreprenören’. Key C: 5 400 m × 2 kr = 10 800 vs 1 800 × 2 = 3 600, exactly three times.

A is Sarvhed’s line and dies on ‘Jag tror ändå att den linjen förlorar, och jag tycker inte att den är riktig’. C dies on ‘Bidraget var orättvist, och jag begär det inte tillbaka – inte heller ett nytt räknat per hushåll’. D dies on ‘Det jag begär är 1,9 kilometer. Låt plogbilen gå ända fram till vändplanen och lägg sträckan i driftbudgeten’ — he wants ploughing to the existing Kvillnäs vändplan, argues against building one at the bridge (‘drygt tio vintrars plogning’), and never asks for a delay (‘Jag har inget att invända mot besparingen’). Key B: ‘Kommunen har alltså haft rätt i sak’ plus the 1,9-kilometre demand.

A dies on ‘Nio plåtar har moln, och även på de korten ligger samma jämna blå himmel över taken’ — colour also where the plate was not empty. C dies: the clouds are on nine plates, not on any card; every card carries ‘samma jämna blå himmel’. D dies on ‘Himlen ändras på varje kort’ — white is the plates’ state (‘På de flesta plåtarna är den en tom vit yta’), not the cards’. Key B.

A dies on absence and on the firm’s own process (‘Fotograferingen skedde med glasplåt’, forty-one plates of its own kept) — no bought-in pictures. B dies on absence — no other publisher is mentioned. C is world-plausible (cards can sit unsold for years) but not in the text: ‘lagret’ in ‘En del hör till lagret’ is glossed by the very next sentence as reprinting — ‘Vidbring tryckte nya upplagor från samma plåt så länge ett motiv gick att sälja’ — and nothing mentions shops or unsold stock; fair, but text-external. Key D restates that sentence and is what explains the 1919 postmark on the magasin demolished in 1911.
